# Scarp Studio v0.0.2-alpha.1 — Windows compiler-integrated IDE (DRAFT)

> **Unpublished release-note candidate.** No tag or GitHub release is authorized by this file. The complete source is consolidated in [draft PR #82 targeting main](https://github.com/scarp-lang/scarp-studio/pull/82). Exact-head CI, manual Windows 11 acceptance, owner merge approval and separate explicit publication approval are still required.

**Experimental, unsigned Windows x64 pre-release candidate** for the Scarp programming language only (`.srp`). It is not a stable IDE. Keep backups of important work and use disposable sources when evaluating the candidate.

## What is planned to be included

- Tauri 2 + React/TypeScript + Monaco Scarp-only editor, syntax highlighting, hover, completion snippets, function outline, starter programs, theme and editor settings. The While/Break/Continue and nested Repeat/While starters embed their exact checked-in `.srp` QA fixtures as static Vite raw imports, so the official compiler compatibility gate tests the actual examples the user receives. Windows case C26 remains NOT RUN.
- Unreleased alpha.17 editor assistance for fixed-array `array_len`/`array_get_or` and preloaded-input `input_boolean`, with versioned hover and completion guidance. These are editor hints, not compiler parsing, and interactive input remains preloaded rather than a live terminal.
- Multiple tabs and source snapshots with dirty indicators; carefully guarded Open, Save, Save As, Save All and Reload from Disk. Deferred Save As selections and pre-save disk checks reject stale source edits, tab-switch ABA, and close/reopen before writing; Save All allows newer edits in later queued tabs. Each completed native write is now followed by a bounded UTF-8 read-back; mismatched or unreadable disk contents fail Save verification without falsely marking the source clean.
- Bounded Scarp project Explorer for the selected root and the immediate `src/`, `tests/` and `examples/` directories. The combined 200-file selection distributes slots across all populated directories rather than hiding `src/main.srp` behind hundreds of root files; an inspected `main.srp` entrypoint also survives an individually crowded directory. Refresh is manual; source reads remain bounded and scoped to the user-selected folder. Regression tests are automated; the crowded-folder GUI acceptance case P34 is still pending.
- Quick Open, Go to Line, open-buffer search, Unicode-safe literal Replace All with preview/confirmation and one-level guarded Undo. These operate on open editor buffers, not arbitrary files across disk.
- Separately installed official **Scarp compiler** for Run and static Verify. Studio can detect candidates without execution and, on first Run, ask for explicit **per-session trust** of the full candidate path before probing or executing. There is no fake Run, bundled compiler, silent installation, background compiler execution or authorization carried over from a previous session.
- Stop during a compiler version/capability probe or a running compiler process. Bounded stdin/prompt input and process-output capture.
- Project Info, Verify Project, Run Project, List Tests and Run Tests when the selected compiler supports the audited CLI. Modified source buffers in the selected project now block every source-backed action, **including read-only List Tests** so a stale saved-disk inventory cannot be presented as current. Project Info remains available with dirty tabs; unrelated projects and untitled tabs do not block saved project work. Windows GUI case P35 remains pending. Structured test output is parsed strictly against both the requested test command and the native compiler exit status; contradictory or stale summaries are rejected while preserving raw output. Test reports are invalidated after selected-project source or Explorer changes.
- **Mid-identifier Monaco completion accuracy (unreleased integration):** a suggestion accepted before the end of an identifier now replaces the existing suffix, while punctuation/unrelated boundaries retain prefix-only replacement. Tests cover both; real Windows GUI case E51 remains NOT RUN.
- **Source-verified declaration outline (unreleased integration):** `qa/windows/08-declaration-outline.srp` now compiles and runs in every pinned alpha.17/18/19 Windows compatibility gate. The front-end outline regression imports this exact `.srp` source (Vite `?raw`) rather than maintaining an unverified duplicate; manual GUI E53 still required.
- **Scarp declaration outline (unreleased integration):** Sidebar and Monaco document symbols now recognize `pub record` and `pub variant` alongside typed `funcra` declarations, with per-type symbols, source-line navigation, CR/LF/CRLF support and a strict 500-entry outline cap. Detection is editor-only and intentionally conservative; manual GUI acceptance E53 NOT RUN.
- **Bounded lexical assistance (unreleased integration):** Monaco completion/hover inspect no more than 16,384 UTF-16 code units before the caret; extraordinarily long single lines suppress assistance rather than repeatedly scanning megabytes on every editor interaction. The source remains editable and runnable; manual E52 NOT RUN.
- Monaco Scarp completions now limit live prefix matching to 128 UTF-16 units and use locale-independent lowercasing for built-in suggestions, including uppercase INPUT_BOOLEAN on Turkish Windows locales (manual E48 NOT RUN).
- Quick Open/Command Palette queries are limited to 256 UTF-16 units, with safe emoji clipping and locale-independent case-insensitive matching across source names and paths. This bounds interactive paste work without changing file permissions or running commands. Windows E47 manual acceptance is NOT RUN.
- Structured diagnostics on failed static Verify, with snapshot-safe Monaco navigation and UTF-16/Unicode column conversion. Valid, same-line bounded JSON-v1 end spans now highlight the complete source range; invalid/missing/multiline/out-of-bounds spans safely fall back to a single Unicode scalar (Windows D18 NOT RUN). Program Input and prompt-mode changes also carry a session-only generation: a delayed first-Run compiler approval refuses to execute an older input snapshot, and completed Run/Run Project output is labeled historical after later input changes without retaining the input text (manual D16 NOT RUN). The completed single-file Run/Verify output retains its exact saved-source generation; subsequent edits, Save As, close/reopen or A→B→A changes mark the retained raw output visibly stale even after diagnostic navigation is withdrawn. Unrelated tab edits do not falsely mark it stale (manual D15 still NOT RUN). When a source or selected project changes during an in-flight compiler command, the completed output is clearly marked as coming from an older snapshot. **A successful completed project command also keeps its source/listing generation**: later project edits, close/reopen or Explorer refresh show an immediate stale warning above the retained raw output while invalidating the old structured test report (manual P38 pending). Unrelated tab changes do not mark the result stale; stale structured errors/test results cannot be applied to the current editor.
- **Compiler auto-discovery (unreleased integration):** a bounded native scan proposes paths in PATH, standard installs and Scarp-named Downloads folders without running any candidate. The user explicitly confirms the exact location before Studio's first compiler probe or source Run. The official alpha.20 ZIP download is a manually clicked browser link, not an automatic installer.
- **Optional Auto Save (unreleased integration):** off by default; configurable 1/3/5-second inactivity delay. Named `.srp` buffers (including background tabs) are saved through external-change checks, exact-revision validation and bounded post-write verification; untitled files never open an automatic Save As dialog. Scheduling pauses during native/compile operations.
- **Read-only disk comparison (unreleased integration):** explicit Compare with Disk reviews the last saved Scarp source snapshot, live editor buffer, and current disk contents using existing 4 MiB scoped UTF-8 reading. Distinguishes unchanged/external/conflicting/matching-buffer states; shows bounded Unicode-safe excerpts but never writes files or implicitly authorizes Reload/Save As. Stale editor sessions cancel comparison. Windows GUI case E43 is NOT RUN.
- **Read-only selected-project search (unreleased integration):** explicit Search Project scans at most 24 already-listed .srp sources with bounded 512 KiB UTF-8 reads and a 2 MiB aggregate accepted UTF-8 byte search budget; scoped native read limits shrink with remaining capacity, and no additional read starts once the budget is full. Dirty already-listed open buffers are selected before clean sources within each root/src/tests/examples group (still only 24 files total); skipped/inaccessible results are labeled incomplete, and stale disk hits never navigate without an exact re-read. Manual Windows GUI acceptance E42 remains NOT RUN.
- **Keyboard tablist navigation (unreleased integration):** ArrowLeft/ArrowRight wraps between open files, Home/End jumps to the first/last tab, and only the active tab participates in normal keyboard tab order. Focus follows selected source; a tab's Close button does not trigger tablist navigation. Actual Windows GUI case E41 remains NOT RUN.
- **Additional source-freshness protection (unreleased integration):** newly inserted dirty source tabs in the selected project invalidate historical project search results and structured project test output, while opening clean tabs solely to inspect sources does not. This future-proofs resumed/batched editor sessions; it does not add automatic session recovery.
- **Project Run budget parity (unreleased integration):** both single-file Run and Run Project explicitly use at most 200,000 interpreter steps and 1,000 print statements, with the same 16 KiB preloaded input cap and existing native timeout. The official compiler smoke must reject the 1001st print with E0018 (manual P39 NOT RUN).
- **Optional visual Monaco controls (unreleased integration):** Settings now includes minimap and whitespace visibility toggles, off by default, strict locally persisted boolean parsing with legacy migration and Restore defaults support. The expanded Settings strip scrolls inside shorter Windows viewports rather than pushing out the editor. Actual Windows 11 GUI acceptance E50 is NOT RUN.
- **Full Settings defaults reset (unreleased integration):** Restore all defaults resets editor font, indentation and wrapping along with Auto Save (off, 3-second idle delay). The Auto Save writer is synchronously revoked before React commits the preference changes; manual Windows E37 validation remains required.
- **Version-prioritized Scarp ZIP discovery (unreleased integration):** a bounded, non-executing scan now orders extracted Scarp-named Downloads folders and versioned Scarp installation folders by numeric version hints, so older alpha.9 does not hide alpha.18 behind the existing four-candidate limit. Folder labels are not trusted version evidence; explicit exact-path approval and the native compiler probe remain required. Rust regression coverage was added; Windows case C24 is NOT RUN.
- **Crowded Downloads scan (unreleased integration):** Scarp-named archive directories are prioritized within a bounded 4096-name lookahead before spending the normal 512-entry per-root processing budget. Native regression coverage is added; manual Windows case C23 is NOT RUN.
- **Scarp compiler download discovery priority (unreleased integration):** Windows Scarp-named extracted Downloads folders are visited **before unbounded PATH entries**, after standard install roots, so 128-root/4096-entry search limits cannot silently omit a newly downloaded official compiler. Explicit per-session trust is still required before any discovered executable is probed or launched.
- **Replace All review guard (unreleased integration):** Auto Save never silently persists the immediate result of confirmed in-buffer Replace All, even when already enabled or enabled later. Only affected named tabs are held for explicit user Save/Save All or Undo; unrelated sources remain eligible for timed saves. Disabling Auto Save during native preflight prevents starting another write. Windows E33–E36 remain manually unverified.
- **Safe Save As tab identity (unreleased integration):** Save As from A.srp to B.srp preserves the existing tab, and reopening original A.srp allocates a different internal tab ID. Commands, edits and closing the reopened tab cannot inadvertently target B.srp. Tested in the state reducer, with Windows 11 case E32 pending manual validation.
- Native source/file read safeguards, concurrent-operation guards, and exact-run Windows artifact SHA-256 validation with tamper and extra-file rejection. Single-file Run/Verify also repeat the bounded saved-source comparison **after** execution: if external edits or deletion are detected, raw output is kept but old diagnostic navigation is blocked.

## Official compiler compatibility

This candidate **does not include or auto-download any compiler**. Windows CI checks separately downloaded, SHA-256-pinned official Scarp CLI archives for `v0.0.6-alpha.10` through `v0.0.6-alpha.15`, plus `v0.0.6-alpha.17` as a backwards-compatibility gate and `v0.0.6-alpha.18` as a separately tested compatibility baseline and `v0.0.6-alpha.19` as an independent compatibility baseline, plus `v0.0.6-alpha.20` as the new proposed compatible compiler. Alpha.16 is not independently covered by this candidate's CI matrix.

The alpha.15 smoke gate validates the published Windows archive's exact hash, version, valid Verify/Run, JSON v1 error coordinates, and Studio's native process service. New alpha.15 ELF64 and compiler-cache changes are Rust embedding / experimental kernel features, **not** new Scarp Studio UI functions. Alpha.15's string-comparison work accounting can reject programs that previously fit narrow work budgets.

The alpha.20 gate independently pins the new published Windows ZIP and repeats existing CLI QA and native execution/discovery checks. The new Linux-only embedding target is not a Windows Studio capability. Alpha.20 compatibility remains subject to exact-head CI and GUI acceptance.

The alpha.19 gate independently checks the published Windows ZIP digest, exec/verify CLI capability guides, Studio's checked-in Run/Verify/Input/JSON QA fixtures, native compiler operation and bounded non-executing discovery. Alpha.19's new callable handles and host usage ledgers belong to Rust embedding and do **not** add Scarp source-level first-class functions or closures to Studio.

The alpha.17 backwards-compatibility gate validates the exact official archive digest, published CLI version, real `array_len`/`array_get_or` execution, preloaded interactive `input_boolean`, JSON v1 diagnostic coordinates, and Studio native Run/Verify. The alpha.18 candidate additionally validates `array_set` immutable snapshots, no-argument `exec` entrypoint discovery, the native service, and the non-executing compiler finder with the new official archive SHA-256 pin. Monaco now offers alpha.18 versioned array update help. These are **compiler compatibility tests**, not a claim that the Studio GUI already offers the new intrinsic completions or automatic compiler discovery.

## Limitations

- Windows 11 x64 first. No Linux/macOS desktop installers in this candidate.
- No semantic Go-to-Definition, verified language server, debugger, generalized terminal or unrestricted recursive workspace search.
- The release remains unsigned and experimental; Windows security warnings must be evaluated, never bypassed on assumption of safety.
- A successful GitHub Actions run **does not** prove Windows GUI behavior or that every filesystem-permission scenario works. Manual checks remain mandatory.
- Native file consistency checks are best-effort, not OS-level atomic snapshots. File symlinks/junctions and external edits still require careful review.
- This candidate is source code and CI artifacts until independently approved; the previously published `v0.0.1-alpha.2` remains editor-only.

## Reviewer checklist before owner approval

- [ ] Review consolidated integration PR #55, stacked PRs #56–#58 and the release-preparation PR that contains this file. Do not merge ancestor branches separately as duplicated changes.
- [ ] Confirm the **exact candidate commit** has green frontend, native Rust, official Scarp alpha.10–alpha.15, alpha.17, alpha.18, alpha.19 and alpha.20 smoke, Windows executable, unsigned NSIS and checksum/tamper checks.
- [ ] Run `npm run check:release-candidate` and `npm run test:release-candidate`. All six manifest versions must match `0.0.2-alpha.1`; these commands do not publish.
- [ ] Download executable, installer and checksum artifacts from **one single green workflow run** and verify them in a clean directory with `scripts/verify-windows-artifacts.ps1` against that run's exact commit.
- [ ] Record actual Windows 11 GUI results for the scenarios in `docs/windows-11-acceptance.md`, including P28–P30, compiler discovery C15–C20, Auto Save E27–E31, Save As/reopen collision case E32, Replace All/Auto Save cases E33–E36, Settings reset E37 and C12.
- [ ] Fix all blocking failures, repeat CI and manual tests after any candidate changes.
- [ ] Obtain distinct, explicit owner approval for merging to `main` and subsequently publishing the **exact approved source commit** as `v0.0.2-alpha.1`.

**No tag, release, installer publication, signing claim or successful Windows GUI acceptance is implied.**
